pending_commit.commit_message: kerberos: Add TgtRenewalScheduler class TgtRenewalScheduler is responsible for scheduling automatic Kerberos ticket-granting-ticket (TGT) renewals. Usually, TGTs are valid for 8-10 hours and can be renewed periodically for a week or 2, which refreshes the validity lifetime each time until the renewal lifetime limit is hit. TgtRenewalScheduler schedules renewal tasks. If the ticket lifetime is 10 hours, it schedules automatic renewals after 6h0m, 8h24m, 9h21m, 9h44m, 9h53m and 9h 57m. If all these attempts failed, it will send a notification that the ticket is about to expire. If the ticket was already expired, e.g. after waking up from a suspended state, it sends out a notification that the ticket has already expired. The class is not used yet. This is done in a follow-up CL. BUG=chromium:952242 TEST=Unit test Change-Id: Ice4ceac8432b6055098e2773ac4baa11632e3bcf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1680417 Tested-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org>

kerberos: Automatically renew Kerberos tickets Uses a TgtRenewalScheduler for each Kerberos account to automatically renew Kerberos tickets. If renewal fails, the code attempts to acquire a fresh ticket if the login password or a previously remembered password are available. If that fails as well, it emits a KerberosTicketExpiring notification 3 minutes before a ticket expires, so Chrome can pop up a notification. BUG=chromium:952242 TEST=Enable KerberosEnabled policy, go to chrome:settings/kerberosAccounts, add an account (e.g. using a chromeadm-lab.com account), add ticket_lifetime=10m to the configuration. Unplug network. Wait 7 minutes. You should eventually see a notification to refresh the ticket. With network plugged in, the ticket should renew and there should be not notification. login: Add --crash-loop-before if we might be in a crash loop In session_manager, when launching a user's Chrome process, see if a quick failure of that process will cause the user to be logged out (because their previous Chrome sessions have failed rapid, that is, because we are in a crash loop). If so, add --crash-loop-before to the Chrome execution. This will cause crash_reporter to upload any crashes immediately instead of writing them to the user directory, which will be locked after the next crash. This is the last functional change needed to enable crash-loop mode! BUG=chromium:857317 TEST=Repeatedly "kill -SEGV" chrome. Eventually got an UploadSingleCrash crash report in crash-staging, just as session_manager logged me out. Change-Id: I18b5d5b150bc7a1e0d56fb815864c6a45bd9cdcb Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1696906 Tested-by: Ian Barkley-Yeung <iby@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Ian Barkley-Yeung <iby@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jeffrey Kardatzke <jkardatzke@google.com>
